image_spec.headline: Between 30% and 40% of the U.S. food supply goes to waste.
image_spec.body: A lot of it is small stuff at home. The half bag of spinach. The last two tortillas.
image_spec.tip: Move the oldest food to the front of the fridge.

posts.caption:
Somewhere between 30% and 40% of the food supply in the U.S. ends up wasted, according to the USDA.

That sounds like a farms-and-trucks problem, and some of it is. But a lot of it happens in our own kitchens. The half bag of spinach. The last two tortillas. The leftovers we swore we'd take for lunch.

One small habit for this week: move the oldest food to the front of the fridge, where you'll actually see it. 🧊

What always gets lost in the back of yours? Tell us in the comments.

#smartshopping #groceryshopping #familymeals #stashsmart #mobilepantry
posts.source_note: USDA, Food Waste FAQs: in the United States, food waste is estimated at between 30-40 percent of the food supply (about 133 billion pounds and $161 billion of food in 2010, based on USDA ERS's estimate of 31 percent food loss at the retail and consumer levels). https://www.usda.gov/foodwaste/faqs

image_spec.headline: Lettuce went up 7.9% in one month. Use every leaf.
image_spec.body: Pantry gives you a heads-up 48 hours before food goes bad, so it gets eaten, not tossed.

posts.caption:
Lettuce went up 7.9% from September to October, according to the latest price report from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Fresh vegetables overall rose 2.2%.

So that bag of greens slowly turning to soup in the crisper drawer stings a little more right now. We've all found one.

That's the moment we're building Pantry alerts for. StashSmart gives you a heads-up 48 hours before something goes bad, so Tuesday's salad actually gets made. 🥫
